title: Cap. V Obj. 6 Sol: Major's consequence wobbles — elect in Christ as members to be united
pass_a_gloss: Solution. The consequence of the Major wobbles. For although the decree of election tends upon a dead man and one lying in the mass of perdition, yet it so tends that it does not decree life to him except insofar as he is considered as a member, according to the good pleasure of the Divine will, to be united to Christ, and to be made alive through Christ. And in this sense, those are elected in Christ who are not yet considered grafted into Christ by faith.
pass_b_english: Sol. The Major's consequence wobbles. The election decree does tend on a dead man lying in the mass of perdition — yet so that it decrees him life only as considered a member, by God's good pleasure, to be united to Christ and made alive through Christ. In that sense they are elected in Christ who are not yet considered grafted into Christ by faith.
source_text: Sol. Vacillat Majoris consequentia. Nam quamvis decretum electionis tendat in hominem mortuum ac in massa perditionis jacentem, ita tamen tendit, ut vitam ei non decernat nisi quatenus consideratur ut membrum, juxta Divinae voluntatis beneplacitum, Christo uniendum, et per Christum vivificandum. Atque hoc sensu, in Christo eliguntur qui nondum per fidem in Christum insiti considerantur.
